title: Claude Certified Developer – Professional (CCDV-P) Study Guide
summary: A source-cited study guide: 25 skill chapters across the 8 domains of the official blueprint, with every factual claim linked to a verbatim quote from its source.
about: A source-cited study guide for the CCDV-P exam, republished in PaNIC Study Room with the author’s permission. Not affiliated with, endorsed or reviewed by Anthropic. Exam-lens boxes are the author’s editorial inference, not official exam content. Reviews were performed by AI models, not human subject-matter experts.

intro.title: Introduction
intro.summary: What the CCDV-P exam measures, how this guide is organized, and how to read its citations.

skills.title: Multi-Agent Orchestration
skills.summary: Decide when a multi-agent design earns its token cost, how to bound fan-out and isolation, and where approvals and cancellation belong.

sections.text: Orchestration patterns and what they cost

skills.objective: Evaluating orchestration patterns for production multi-agent designs and inter-agent failures, including supervisor/worker hierarchies, parallel subagent dispatch, delegation and context-isolation boundaries, inter-agent communication, and human-in-the-loop and approval flows.

skills.title: Durable Execution and State Management
skills.summary: Decide which state a resumed agent must reload, which side effects need idempotency guards, and how to survive a model version change.
skills.objective: Applying session persistence, checkpointing, resumability, and memory architecture patterns to long-running agents that must survive interruption, restart, and model version change.

skills.title: Architecture Selection at Scale
skills.summary: Decide between workflow and agentic patterns from measured cost, reliability, and quality data, and pick the execution layer and shared standards.

sections.text: Workflow, agent, and multi-agent are control-flow choices
Measure the running system before you change it
A hypothetical: workflow versus bounded agent

skills.objective: Evaluating production cost, reliability, and quality data to decide whether to evolve a running system between workflow and agentic patterns, and selecting the agent harness, framework, and reusable-pattern standards a team should adopt.

skills.title: Context and Memory Architecture
skills.summary: Choose context, memory, tool-loading, and cache policies for a long-running agent.

sections.text: Context editing: pruning that leaves history intact
Persistent memory: state that outlives the window
Keeping large tool catalogs out of the window
Worked example: a deferred catalog and a mid-run escalation

skills.objective: Evaluating context-policy options for long-running agents approaching context limits or cost ceilings, including context compaction and editing, persistent memory, cache-safe instruction changes mid-conversation, and tool-use techniques that keep large tool catalogs out of the context window.

domains.title: Production Integration, Reliability, and Knowledge Grounding

skills.title: Reliability Engineering for Claude Services
skills.summary: Decide which failure signal a Claude response carries, then choose the matching recovery: fail fast, budgeted retry, stop-reason handling, or parity-checked failover.

sections.text: Read the signal before you react
Telling rate limits, refusals, and context-window stops apart

skills.objective: Evaluating and applying resilience patterns for production Claude integrations, including retry and backoff design, circuit breakers, graceful degradation, and cross-model, cross-region, and cross-platform fallbacks that distinguish rate limits from safety refusals from context-window stops while respecting per-platform feature parity.

skills.title: Scale and Throughput Management
skills.summary: Decide whether requests, input tokens, output tokens, queueing, tenant caps, or batch economics constrain a Claude workload, and pick the matching remedy.

sections.text: Read limits from the response headers
Tiers, model buckets, and version drift
Capacity planning and the binding constraint

skills.objective: Analyzing rate-limit strategy, queueing and backpressure, batch pipeline design, multi-tenant quota and isolation, and capacity planning for high-volume Claude workloads, and identifying whether rate limits, token throughput, or batch economics is the binding constraint.

skills.title: Production MCP and Change Management
skills.summary: Decide which layer of a running agent changed — protocol, endpoint, credential, tool schema, model, prompt, or route — and release it as one tested bundle.
skills.objective: Applying production MCP operation and change-management practice to MCP server deployments, model version migrations, and prompt updates, including remote MCP deployment and authentication, tool and schema versioning, migration testing against breaking behavior changes, platform-specific configuration parity and gateway/routing architectures, prompt versioning, and progressive rollout with rollback.

skills.title: Retrieval and Knowledge Grounding at Scale
skills.summary: Decide between direct context, indexed RAG, and agentic search, and locate a retrieval-quality failure at the stage where evidence is lost.

sections.text: Grounding contracts: citations and source attribution

skills.skillTitle: Retrieval and Knowledge Grounding at Scale
skills.objective: Evaluating retrieval architecture for knowledge-grounded production applications, including agentic search versus RAG tradeoffs, chunking and embedding strategy, hybrid search, and reranking, and designing grounding practices such as source citation, uncertainty declaration, and confidence signals, and diagnosing retrieval-quality failures by stage.

skills.title: Telemetry and Instrumentation
skills.summary: Decide which signals, token sources, content-capture settings, and propagation hops a production Claude system needs under privacy constraints.

sections.text: Distributed traces for agent loops and tool calls

skills.objective: Applying instrumentation practice to production Claude systems under debuggability and privacy requirements, including distributed traces for agent loops and tool calls, token and cost metrics, cache-performance diagnostics, grounding and reasoning traceability, structured log events, and content-capture configuration under privacy constraints such as zero-data-retention.

skills.title: Production Monitoring and Alerting
skills.summary: Decide which SLIs an LLM service needs, how to alert on burn rates and spend, and how to separate quality drift, cache loss, and model shifts.

sections.text: How it works: signals, budgets, and burn rate
Latency, stop reasons, and quality SLIs

skills.objective: Analyzing production signals from LLM-backed services to define service level indicators (SLIs) and SLOs, design alerting and dashboards (including token and cost telemetry), and detect quality drift, behavioral regressions, and anomalous usage, including drift after model updates.

skills.title: Trace Analysis at Scale
skills.summary: Decide what to sample, aggregate, and compare so trace data quantifies systemic agent failures instead of illustrating anecdotes.
skills.objective: Analyzing high-volume trace data using sampling strategies, aggregation, and failure-cohort analysis to surface and quantify systemic issues that are not visible in individual traces.

skills.title: Complex Failure Diagnosis
skills.summary: Decide whether a production agent failure came from the model, the harness, tools, or data by replaying evidence layer by layer.

sections.text: How it works: the evidence chain
Model, harness, tool, or data: isolating the origin

skills.objective: Analyzing evidence from complex production failures, including multi-turn, multi-agent, and non-deterministic failures, to isolate the problem origin among model output, agent harness, tools, and data, including model refusals as a failure class and retrieval-grounding failures.

skills.title: Incident Response and Learning Loops
skills.summary: Decide triage order, containment, rollback, and communication during an LLM outage, and convert the incident into evals, alerts, and postmortems.

sections.text: Incident command: roles, record, and communication
Triage: vendor outage, quality regression, or your incident
Learning loop: postmortem, regression evals, monitoring

skills.objective: Evaluating incident-response options during an LLM-system outage or quality regression, including triage, mitigation, rollback, and communication, and converting the incident into regression evaluations, monitoring coverage, and postmortem findings.

skills.title: Evaluation System Design
skills.summary: Decide how to build offline eval suites, grade agent behavior, set CI/CD gate thresholds, and release prompt, model, and agent changes.

sections.text: Release criteria for prompt, model, and agent changes

skills.objective: Evaluating and designing offline evaluation systems for Claude applications, including golden sets, regression suites, behavioral checks, CI/CD evaluation gates, retrieval precision and groundedness metrics, and release criteria for prompt, model, and agent changes, and maintaining suite validity over time against contamination, saturation, and coverage gaps.

skills.title: LLM-as-Judge Engineering
skills.summary: Decide whether a Claude judge is calibrated enough to gate releases: rubric design, order swapping, inter-rater reliability, and drift control.

sections.text: Grading mode: pointwise, pairwise, and reference-guided
Calibrating the judge against human labels

skills.objective: Analyzing LLM-as-judge evaluator quality against human-labeled data, including calibration, rubric design, bias and position effects, inter-rater reliability, and judge drift across model versions.

skills.title: Online Quality Measurement
skills.summary: Choose sampling, experiment, feedback, and metric designs that measure quality on live Claude application traffic.

sections.text: Worked example: sizing and reading an A/B test
Production data sources and API details

skills.objective: Analyzing quality on live production traffic using online evaluation techniques, including live-traffic sampling, A/B testing, feedback loops, and metric selection matched to task type (extraction, generation, agentic, retrieval-grounded).

domains.title: Cost and Latency Optimization at Scale

skills.title: Cost Architecture at Scale
skills.summary: Decide which cost lever to pull—caching, model routing, batch offload, or budget enforcement—from usage data and per-tenant economics.
skills.objective: Evaluating fleet-level optimization strategies using usage and cost data, including cost modeling and forecasting, model routing and cascades across the Claude model family, caching strategy and cache diagnostics, batch-versus-realtime economics, and per-tenant budget enforcement.

skills.title: Latency Engineering
skills.summary: Decide which latency lever to pull—streaming, parallel tools, cache checkpoints, effort, model, fast mode—from TTFT and TTLT evidence.

sections.text: Effort, model choice, and capacity tiers

skills.objective: Analyzing the latency profile of a Claude application against a latency target, distinguishing time-to-first-token from total latency, and applying streaming, parallel tool execution, cache checkpointing, and effort-level tuning.

skills.title: Runtime Guardrail Systems
skills.summary: Decide which layer — hook, permission rule, sandbox, approval gate, classifier, or refusal branch — must enforce each production risk.

sections.text: The permission pipeline and rule order
Input filtering, output filtering, and PII redaction
Tuning false positives and false negatives

skills.objective: Evaluating layered guardrail architectures against a production agent’s risk profile, including input/output filtering, PII redactors, hook-based policy enforcement, destructive-action prevention, sandboxing that grants tool and web access without exposing production systems, approval gates, refusal handling and safety fallbacks, deterministic enforcement for irreversible actions, and false-positive/false-negative tuning.

skills.title: Threat Defense and Adversarial Testing for Agentic Systems
skills.summary: Decide which injection, exfiltration, and MCP failure mode an agent faces, and place the deterministic control that breaks it outside the model.

sections.text: Attack surface: untrusted content reaching the model
The lethal trifecta and its exfiltration paths
Worked example: injection inside an MCP tool result
Unsafe autonomy and the sandbox boundary

skills.skillTitle: Threat Defense and Adversarial Testing for Agentic Systems
skills.objective: Analyzing the attack surface of tool-using agents that process untrusted content, including prompt injection, tool and memory poisoning, data exfiltration paths, unsafe-autonomy conditions, and the high-risk combination of private data access, untrusted input, and external communication, and applying defense-in-depth mitigations, red-team exercise design, and secure MCP configuration, drawing on the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework and its Generative AI Profile.

skills.title: Identity, Secrets, and Audit at Scale
skills.summary: Decide which credential a Claude workload holds, how its tools are permitted and authorized, and which audit source proves what happened.

sections.text: How a Claude workload gets an identity
Least privilege for tools and MCP

skills.skillTitle: Identity, Secrets, and Audit at Scale
skills.objective: Applying enterprise identity and secrets practice to production Claude deployments, including agent identity, workload identity federation replacing static API keys, credential and secrets management, least-privilege tool permissioning, and audit logging of security-relevant agent actions.

domains.title: Agent Fleet Operations for Software Delivery

skills.title: Parallel Agent Orchestration for Engineering Work
skills.summary: Choose a parallel topology, isolate and merge agent edits safely, size task decomposition, and diagnose fleet failures from Claude Code telemetry.
skills.skillTitle: Parallel Agent Orchestration for Engineering Work
skills.objective: Evaluating parallel fan-out patterns for large engineering tasks, including parallel agents on isolated worktrees, task decomposition, and merge and conflict strategy, and diagnosing fleet-level failure modes from fleet telemetry.

skills.title: Verification and AI Code Review Operations
skills.summary: Decide which checks run before a pull request, how to calibrate an AI reviewer in shadow mode, and where human approvals belong.

sections.text: Review surfaces: managed, local, and CI
Convergence when the author is an agent

skills.skillTitle: Verification and AI Code Review Operations
skills.objective: Analyzing verification operations in delivery pipelines where generation outpaces review, including AI code review introduced in shadow mode, calibration against human review before merge gating, and human oversight design.

skills.title: Unattended and Event-Driven Agent Operations
skills.summary: Choose goal, schedule, or event triggers for Claude Code runs, and design their bounds, checkpoints, notifications, and escalation.

sections.text: Event responders and CI first response

skills.objective: Applying unattended-operation patterns to goal- or schedule-driven engineering tasks, including agents running toward goals, on schedules, or as event-driven responders such as CI/CD incident first response, with checkpointing, notification, and escalation design.

skills.title: Organization-Wide Coding Agent Configuration
skills.summary: Decide which Claude Code policy layer enforces permissions, MCP servers, telemetry, gateway routing, and shared Skills across a fleet.

sections.text: Server-managed settings and their skip rule
Governance for plugins, Skills, and shared prompts

skills.objective: Applying enterprise configuration for organizations adopting coding agents, including managed settings and policies, MCP allowlists, telemetry, gateway routing, and governance with a quality and safety bar for sharing prompts, Skills, and MCP servers across teams.
